paper_title: Development of a General and Practical Iron Nitrate/TEMPO-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Alcohols to Aldehydes/Ketones: Catalysis with Table Salt

questions.question: In Scheme 1 and the accompanying tables the label 'Hex-n' is used repeatedly. What does 'Hex-n' refer to in this paper?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Hex-n denotes an n‑hexyl substituent (the n‑hexyl group used in 3-(n-hexyl)-1,2-octadien-4-ol / corresponding substrates).

questions.question: In the large-scale experiment (Eq. 2) the paper oxidizes 1-phenylethanol. What is the product obtained from oxidation of 1-phenylethanol in that large-scale reaction (give the product name reported in the paper)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Phenyl methyl ketone (acetophenone) is formed from 1-phenylethanol (reported as the product in Eq. (2)).

questions.question: Which solvent was selected as optimal for the aerobic oxidation of 3-(n-hexyl)-1,2-octadien-4-ol in the optimization studies (Table 1 and related text)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 1,2-Dichloroethane (DCE) was selected as the optimal solvent.

questions.question: Referring to the additive screen (Table 3), which additive gave a higher yield for the aerobic oxidation screening of 3-(n-hexyl)-1,2-octadien-4-ol: NaCl (entry 5) or NaNO2 (entry 1)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: NaCl (entry 5) gave the higher yield: NaCl showed 100% conversion and 72% yield, whereas NaNO2 (entry 1) showed 55% conversion and 35% yield.

questions.question: What isolated yield (%) of phenyl methyl ketone (acetophenone) was obtained in the 4.0 mmol (large-scale) oxidation of 1-phenylethanol reported in Eq. (2)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 91% isolated yield of phenyl methyl ketone (acetophenone).
